UAE Employment Visa (Work Permit + Residence Visa)
rows.description: Standard employer-sponsored work pathway for private sector foreign employees. Employer applies via MOHRE for work permit; employee enters on Entry Permit and obtains Residence Visa within 60 days. Governed by Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021.

rows.name_en: UAE Golden Visa (Long-Term Residence — 5 or 10 years)
rows.description: Long-term renewable residence visa for investors, entrepreneurs, scientists, exceptional talent, outstanding students and humanitarian pioneers. No employer sponsor required. Valid 5 or 10 years depending on category.

rows.name_en: UAE Green Visa (5-Year Self-Sponsored Skilled Worker)
rows.description: Five-year self-sponsored residence visa for highly skilled employees, freelancers, and investors. No employer sponsor required. Minimum salary AED 15,000/month for skilled employees or AED 360,000/year income for freelancers. Bachelor's degree or equivalent required.

rows.name_en: UAE Virtual Work (Digital Nomad) Visa — 1 Year Renewable
rows.description: One-year renewable residence visa for remote workers employed by entities outside the UAE. Minimum income USD 3,500/month. Health insurance mandatory. Self-sponsored; no UAE employer required. Can sponsor family for the same period.

Resident sponsors spouse, children, and parents. Minimum salary AED 4,000/month (or AED 3,000 + employer accommodation) to sponsor spouse and children. Sponsoring parents requires AED 20,000/month. Sons sponsored to age 25; daughters until marriage.

Residence visa for international students enrolled at accredited UAE universities or colleges. Sponsored by the institution or a resident parent. Valid 1 year, renewable annually. Outstanding students may qualify for the 10-year Golden Visa.

rows.name_en: Emirates ID (National Identity Card — Mandatory for All Residents)
rows.description: Mandatory identity document for all UAE residents, issued by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP). Must be obtained after residence visa is stamped. Required for banking, healthcare, driving licence, and all government services.

rows.name_en: Mandatory Employer-Provided Health Insurance (Dubai & Abu Dhabi)
rows.description: Dubai: Law No. 11 of 2013 requires all residents to hold valid health insurance; employers must cover employees. Abu Dhabi: Law No. 23 of 2005 (HAAD/DOH mandate) requires employer-provided coverage for expat employees via approved insurers including DAMAN. Minimum annual benefit limit AED 150,000.

rows.name_en: UAE Tax Regime — No Personal Income Tax; 9% Corporate Tax; 5% VAT
rows.description: UAE levies zero personal income tax on individuals. Corporate tax of 9% on taxable profits exceeding AED 375,000 applies from June 2023. VAT at 5% introduced January 2018. Expats may still owe taxes in their home country (e.g., US citizens). No social security contributions for expat employees.

rows.name_en: End of Service Gratuity (EOSB) — Mandatory Employer Obligation
rows.description: Under UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021), employers must pay end-of-service gratuity on termination after one year of service. Calculated on basic salary: 21 days per year for first 5 years, 30 days per year thereafter. Applies to all private sector employees regardless of nationality.

rows.name_en: Ejari Tenancy Registration — Dubai (Mandatory for Rent Contracts)
rows.description: All tenancy contracts in Dubai must be registered in the Ejari system managed by the Dubai Land Department (DLD). Required for utility connections (DEWA), visa processing, and legal enforceability. Registration fee approximately AED 215 + VAT. Required document for employer-provided accommodation.

rows.name_en: UAE Labour Ban (Work Permit Restriction for Policy Violations)
rows.description: Under Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, a one-year labour ban (restriction on new work permit) may be imposed by MOHRE on employees who resign without serving the required notice period or violate labour regulations. Pre-2021 automatic bans have been significantly reformed; ban is no longer automatic for all resignations.

rows.name_en: UAE Blue Visa — 10-Year Residency for Environmental Sustainability Leaders
rows.description: Launched 2025. Ten-year renewable residency for individuals making exceptional contributions to environmental conservation, climate science, and sustainability. No property investment required. Initial 180-day multiple-entry exploration visa issued on approval, transitioning to full 10-year residency.

EU/EFTA Notification Procedure for Short-Term Work (≤90 days)
rows.notes: Covers employed EU/EFTA nationals working for Swiss employers up to 3 months per calendar year, and posted workers / self-employed service providers from EU/EFTA. Online notification via easygov.swiss. No permit required.

rows.name_en: EU/EFTA L Permit — Short-Term Residence (3–12 months)
rows.notes: Issued for employment contracts between 3 and 12 months. Permit validity matches contract duration. Issued by cantonal migration office. Also available to EU/EFTA job seekers (no entitlement to social assistance).

rows.name_en: EU/EFTA B Permit — Residence Permit (≥12 months or unlimited)
rows.notes: 5-year validity, renewable. Issued for employment contracts of at least 12 months or of unlimited duration, or for self-employed EU/EFTA nationals. Also available to economically inactive EU/EFTA nationals with sufficient financial means and health insurance.

Available after 5 years regular uninterrupted residence to nationals of treaty countries (Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, EFTA states). No time restrictions once granted. Not available to all EU member states.

EU/EFTA self-employed persons receive B permit valid 5 years if they demonstrate existence of effective self-employed activity. No labour-market test required. Must show sufficient financial means and health insurance.

Issued for 1 year, annually renewable until studies completed. Must show admission to state-recognised institution and ability to self-support. May work up to 15 hrs/week after 6 months of study. Parents cannot be sponsored by student permit holders.

Under AFMP. Employees may bring spouse, children under 21 (or dependent), and dependent parents (not available to students). No income test for employees; self-employed and inactive persons must show sufficient financial means. Family members have full work rights regardless of nationality. Accommodation must reflect typical Swiss living conditions.

Applies to all non-EU/EFTA nationals including UK (post-Brexit), India, USA, Turkey, Brazil, China, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Serbia, Sri Lanka, Eritrea. Quota set annually by Federal Council. Only managers, specialists, and qualified workers admitted. Employer must apply on behalf of employee. Labour-market priority test required.

Employer submits to cantonal authority → cantonal preliminary decision → SEM national-level review → SEM decision → visa issued by cantonal authority to Swiss representation abroad → employee enters → registers at commune within 14 days → may start work. Processing time: 6–8 weeks.

rows.name_en: Third-Country Intra-Company Transfer — Senior Manager / Essential Specialist
rows.notes: Precedence rules (labour-market priority test) do not apply to operational transfers of senior managers and essential specialists within international companies. Still subject to quotas and FNIA admission requirements.

Exception to precedence rules for individuals pursuing research or doctoral studies at accredited Swiss higher education institutions. Post-graduation: 6-month job search permit available without precedence-rule evidence requirement if significant academic or economic interest.

Must demonstrate that self-employment will have a lasting positive impact on Swiss labour market. Requires comprehensive documentation: business plan, market analysis, workforce projections, commercial registration details. Subject to quota and FNIA. Much stricter than EU/EFTA path.

Must show admission to state-recognised Swiss institution, proof of financial self-support, and health insurance. Permit issued for duration of studies. May work max 15 hrs/week after first 6 months of study (employer must apply, university must confirm compatibility). Post-study: 6-month job search permit available.

rows.name_en: Third-Country Post-Study Job Search Permit (6 months)
rows.notes: Third-country graduates of Swiss higher education institutions may remain 6 months to seek employment matching their qualifications. No precedence-rule evidence required. Must have graduated from recognised Swiss university or university of applied sciences.

Under FNIA. Stricter than EU/EFTA route. B permit holders may bring spouse and children. L permit holders require separate employer application for spouse to work. Governed by FNIA Art. 26 ASEO. Income and housing conditions apply. FNIA directives (German/French/Italian only) provide full detail.

Since 1 January 2021, UK nationals are third-country nationals. Must apply for permit before taking up employment. FNIA and ASEO apply. Acquired rights agreement covers those residing in CH before 31 Dec 2020. Services Mobility Agreement (SMA) for certain service providers.

All foreign nationals must register with commune (Einwohnerkontrolle/contrôle des habitants) within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals must register before taking up work. Third-country nationals may not start work until after registration. Apply at commune office of place of residence.

All persons residing in Switzerland for more than 3 months must take out Swiss health insurance (Krankenkasse) under KVG/LAMal. Must choose a Swiss health insurer. Mandatory; non-compliance results in canton assigning an insurer. Premiums vary by canton and insurer.

All employees and self-employed persons must register with AHV (Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung / Old-Age and Survivors Insurance). Employer registers employee and deducts AHV contributions from salary (employee and employer each contribute approx. 5.3%). Self-employed register directly with cantonal AHV compensation fund.

Biometric residence permit card (credit-card format with chip for third-country nationals) issued by cantonal migration office after commune registration and permit application. Chip contains two digital fingerprints and facial image. L, B, and C permit categories covered.

rows.name_en: Young Professionals / Internship Program (TC, selected countries)
rows.notes: Available to nationals of 15 specific countries including USA (but not India, China, Brazil, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Serbia, Sri Lanka, Eritrea, Turkey). Max 18-month permit. Must work in learned profession. Quota applies. Application submitted in home country.

rows.description: EU, EEA, and Swiss nationals exercise free movement rights and do not require an IND residence permit to live or work in the Netherlands. They must register at their local municipality (gemeente) within 4 months of arrival. Registration in the BRP (Basisregistratie Personen) results in automatic BSN assignment.

Non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals may apply for a Highly Skilled Migrant residence permit if employed by an IND-recognised sponsor at or above the applicable salary threshold. The employer (recognised sponsor) submits the application. The permit is linked to the employment contract and is valid up to 5 years.

The IND publishes annual salary thresholds for the kennismigrant route. For 2026: aged 30+: €5,942/month gross; under 30: €4,357/month gross; reduced rate (within 3 years of graduation or completing research): €3,122/month gross. Salary must also be market-rate for the role.

rows.name_en: Highly Skilled Migrant — Application Process and Fees
rows.description: The recognised sponsor submits the application (online via Business Portal or by post using Form 7511) and pays the application fee of €423. The IND must decide within 90 days. After approval, the applicant collects an MVV (entry visa) at the Dutch embassy/consulate within 3 months. The MVV is valid for 90 days. Upon entry, a VVR (residence permit card) is collected at an IND desk.

Non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals with a higher-education diploma (programme of at least 3 years), or 5 years of relevant experience at higher-education level (or 3 years for IT professionals within the last 7 years), may apply for an EU Blue Card. Employment contract must be at least 6 months. Employer must carry out economic activity and not have been fined in the past 5 years for listed labour violations.
Standard rate: €5,942/month gross. Reduced criterion for recent graduates (within 3 years of completion): €4,754/month gross. These thresholds are published annually by the IND.

rows.name_en: EU Blue Card — Application Process and Fees
rows.description: Application fee: €423. Processing time: 30 days (recognised sponsor or simultaneous family application), 45 days (current permit holders for paid work), or 90 days (all others). Permit valid up to 5 years; valid until 3 months after employment contract ends.

For recent graduates/researchers who completed a degree or conducted scientific research within the past 3 years. Qualifying paths include: scientific research in NL, Erasmus Mundus joint master, accredited bachelor/master at Dutch institution, post-master (10+ months), or master/doctoral at top-200 foreign institution (ranked by at least 2 of Times Higher Education, QS, ShanghaiRanking). Cannot have previously held an orientation year permit for the same programme.

rows.name_en: Orientation Year — Application Process and Fees
rows.description: Fee: €254. IND must decide within 90 days. Permit valid for 1 year — cannot be extended. Work freely permitted without TWV during orientation year. Foreign degree holders from top-200 institutions must demonstrate English proficiency (IELTS 6.0 minimum or equivalent). After finding work, must transition to kennismigrant, startup, or self-employed permit.

For managers, specialists, or trainees being transferred by their employer to a Netherlands branch of the same company. Must have worked for the company abroad for at least 3 months. Transfer period must exceed 90 days. Salary must meet highly skilled migrant thresholds. Employment conditions must comply with Dutch law. Maximum transfer: 3 years (managers/specialists) or 1 year (trainees). NL branch must not have been set up solely to facilitate EU transfers.

rows.name_en: ICT Permit — Application Process and Fees
rows.description: Fee: €423. IND must decide within 90 days (may be extended). UWV advice period up to 5 weeks. MVV appointment within 3 months of approval. TB test required within 3 months of permit receipt. Recognised sponsors apply online; others by post.

Applicant must play an active role (beyond shareholder/financier), be registered in the Chamber of Commerce, have an innovative business idea (new product/service/technology/method to the Netherlands), and possess a step-by-step business plan. Must have a RVO-listed facilitator who: has startup mentoring experience, is financially healthy, holds no majority interest in the startup, is not a close relative (within 3rd degree), and has an internal deputy.

rows.name_en: Startup Permit — Application Process and Fees
rows.description: Fee: €423. IND must decide within 90 days. Permit valid for 1 year maximum — cannot be extended; must transition to self-employed permit. MVV required within 3 months of decision. Income must be demonstrated via Dutch bank account or facilitator financing.

For non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals conducting research (paid, unpaid with grant, or doctoral) at an IND-recognised research institution. Must hold a higher-education degree providing access to doctoral programmes. Requires a valid employment contract or host agreement specifying research title, duration, funding, and start/end dates.

rows.name_en: Researcher Permit — Application Process and Fees
rows.description: Fee: €254 (paid by employer via direct debit). IND must decide within 60 days. Permit valid for contract duration up to 5 years maximum. Income threshold: €1,635.90/month without holiday allowance (2026 figure for researchers). Work permitted without restrictions. MVV and VVR issued together on positive decision.

Non-EU/EEA/Swiss students at accredited (NVAO or EQAR) Dutch universities or HBO institutions. Educational institution must be an IND-recognised sponsor and submit the application. Applicant must be enrolled full-time, meet income/living cost requirements, and make sufficient academic progress (at least 50% of study credits per year).

rows.name_en: Study Permit — Application Process and Fees
rows.description: Fee: €254. IND must decide within 60 days. Institution submits application on behalf of student. MVV appointment within 3 months of decision. TB test required within 3 months of permit receipt. Student work allowance: up to 16 hours per week as employee, or full-time during June, July, August. Self-employed work permitted (no hour cap) with Chamber of Commerce registration. Foreign documents must be legalised and translated to Dutch, English, French, or German.

For spouses, registered partners, or unmarried partners of a Dutch national or valid residence permit holder. Both parties must be 21+ (exception: if married before arrival to NL, then 18+). Relationship must be verifiable. Partners must be registered at same municipal address. Sponsor must meet income threshold (€2,337/month without holiday allowance for 2026). Partner must not pose danger to public order or national security.

rows.name_en: Partner Permit — Application Process and Fees
rows.description: Fee: €254. IND must decide within 90 days. MVV valid for 90 days after approval. Permit validity: 5 years (if sponsor is Dutch/permanent resident) or matches sponsor's permit expiration. Civic integration exam may be required abroad before MVV. TB test required on arrival. Antecedents Certificate (form 7601) required for partners over 12.

For children under 18 joining a parent in the Netherlands who holds Dutch nationality or a valid Dutch residence permit. Parent must have lived in NL for at least 1 year with valid permit (exceptions apply). Child must not be married/in partnership. Consent required from the other custodial parent if remaining abroad. Child must not pose threat to public order or national security.

rows.name_en: Minor Child Permit — Application Process and Fees
rows.description: Fee: €85. IND must decide within 90 days. MVV required — appointment at Dutch embassy/consulate within 3 months of decision. MVV valid for 90 days. Foreign documents must be legalised and translated to Dutch, English, French, or German.

The MVV is a long-stay entry visa issued at a Dutch embassy or consulate. It is required for most non-EU applicants before entering the Netherlands for stays exceeding 90 days. The IND grants MVV alongside the residence permit decision; applicant then makes an appointment at the relevant Dutch diplomatic post within 3 months. The MVV is valid for 90 days. Passport must be valid for at least 6 more months. EU nationals do not require an MVV.

Employers, educational institutions, and research organisations must be registered as a recognised sponsor with the IND in order to apply for residence permits on behalf of highly skilled migrants, students, and researchers. A publicly searchable register is maintained by the IND and updated monthly. Cost of recognition: €5,080 (standard) or €2,539 (small business ≤50 persons or exchange purposes).

All residents (EU and non-EU) must register in the BRP (Basisregistratie Personen) at their local municipality (gemeente). Registration triggers assignment of a BSN (Burgerservicenummer / Citizen Service Number), which is required for employment, banking, health insurance, and government services. EU citizens must register within 4 months of arrival. Non-EU permit holders typically register immediately after arrival.

Every person who lives or works in the Netherlands is legally obliged to take out standard health insurance (basisverzekering). Covers GP consultations, hospital treatment, and prescription medication. Insurers must accept any applicant for standard insurance and charge the same premium regardless of age or health. Children under 18 are covered without additional premium. Supplemental insurance is optional. A dedicated helpline (zorgverzekeringslijn.nl) exists for those coming from abroad.

DigiD is the Dutch government's digital identity system, enabling secure login to government services (tax authority, healthcare, municipalities). It requires a BSN for registration. Login methods include: DigiD app, SMS verification, username/password, or identity document scan. Available as a mobile app (iOS and Android).

Ukrainians displaced by the conflict may be entitled to Temporary Protection under the EU Temporary Protection Directive. Under TP status in the Netherlands, holders may live and work without a separate IND work permit. TP status is reviewed and renewed periodically — current status should be verified at ind.nl/en/situation-ukraine. Ukrainians may also apply for regular IND permits (study, kennismigrant) if eligible.

rows.name_en: Syria / Iran — Regular vs Asylum Routes
rows.description: Syrian and Iranian nationals may use regular IND immigration routes (study permit, kennismigrant, researcher, etc.) if they have valid travel documents and meet standard eligibility criteria. Asylum/protection routes are separately handled by the IND asylum department. For professional/student personas, the regular permit routes documented in this knowledge base apply. For asylum-related information, refer to ind.nl/en/asylum.

rows.name_en: UK Nationals Post-Brexit — Third Country Status
rows.description: Since 1 January 2021, UK nationals are treated as third-country (non-EU) nationals in the Netherlands. They no longer benefit from EU free movement. UK nationals must apply for IND residence permits (kennismigrant, study, family, etc.) under the same rules as other non-EU nationals. MVV is required for stays exceeding 90 days.

The sponsoring resident must demonstrate sufficient income for family reunification. 2026 thresholds: spouse/unmarried partner — €2,337/month (without holiday allowance) or €2,523.96 (with holiday allowance); single parent with child — €1,635.90/month (without holiday allowance) or €1,766.77 (with holiday allowance). Note: students sponsoring family face additional constraints — see study financing thresholds.

rows.official_process_note: Submit online at skatteetaten.no — requires passport scan upload. Can be completed in the same Skatteetaten portal session as the tax card (skattekort).

rows.official_process_note: Requested in the same Skatteetaten portal session as the D-number. Must be active before the first payroll run — otherwise 50% emergency withholding applies.

rows.official_process_note: Initiated by the French employer in France (via CPAM / Net-Entreprises) — NOT a Norwegian process. Should be requested at least 4 weeks before the posting starts.
rows.source_version: Your Europe 'Standard forms for social security rights' — Last checked 15/06/2026

rows.name_en: Move-Abroad Notice to the National Register (flyttemelding)
rows.official_process_note: Required for any move outside the Nordic countries intended to last 6 months or more. Folkeregisterloven § 6-3 requires the notice BEFORE departure, and Skatteetaten only takes it shortly beforehand (skatteetaten.no reads "tidligst 31 dager før du flytter", checked 2026-08-14; older guidance says 14 days); filed later it registers from the date it is received, so file retrospectively if you have already left. Reporting the move does NOT end your Norwegian tax liability — that is a separate determination (step 2).
rows.source_version: Folkeregisterforskriften (FOR-2017-07-14-1201), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret FOR-2025-12-17-2639

rows.name_en: Tax Card Close-Out and Exit-Year Tax Return (skattekort / utflytting)
rows.official_process_note: Close out the skattekort with the final Norwegian payroll run, then file the exit-year skattemelding in the spring of the following year (ordinary deadline 30 April) — from abroad, which needs working BankID (step 4). Latent share gains may trigger utflyttingsskatt (exit tax). Keep one Norwegian bank account open until the exit-year tax settlement has cleared.
rows.source_version: Skatteloven (LOV-1999-03-26-14), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret LOV-2026-06-23-66

rows.name_en: End of folketrygden Membership and HELFO Health Cover
rows.name_no: Avslutning av medlemskap i folketrygden og HELFO-dekning
rows.official_process_note: Membership of folketrygden and HELFO cover end in step with the social-security determination — a gap leaves you uncovered, an overlap risks double contributions. Ask HELFO about an S1 handover to French CPAM so the coverage gap is as short as possible, and notify NAV of any active benefits (barnetrygd, sykepenger).
rows.source_version: Folketrygdloven (LOV-1997-02-28-19), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret LOV-2026-06-19-45 / LOV-2026-06-23-65

rows.name_en: Preserve BankID and Digital Access Before Deregistration
rows.name_no: Sikre BankID og digital tilgang før utflytting registreres
rows.official_process_note: Sequencing trap — settle this BEFORE the move notice in step 1 takes effect: deregistration can disable the BankID you still need for the exit-year skattemelding, Altinn and your Norwegian bank. Confirm with the bank in writing what happens to BankID after emigration and which mobile number it will be tied to.

rows.name_en: Proof of Address in France (justificatif de domicile)
rows.official_process_note: Nearly every French registration hangs off this — do it first. With your own lease or purchase: a recent utility bill (facture EDF / eau), the lease (bail), or a tax notice. Hosted by family or friends: the package is an attestation d’hébergement signed by the host + the host’s own proof of address + a copy of the host’s ID.
rows.source_version: Service-Public fiche F14807 'Quel justificatif de domicile présenter ?' — Vérifié le 19 mai 2026

rows.name_en: French Health Cover Registration (CPAM / carte vitale)
rows.name_no: Registrering for fransk helsedekning (CPAM / carte vitale)
rows.official_process_note: File the opening-of-rights dossier with your local CPAM as soon as you have a proof of address. A numéro de sécurité sociale (NIR) is issued first; the carte vitale follows by post. Start immediately — you are between systems from the day HELFO cover ends until CPAM confirms.
rows.source_version: Service-Public fiche F265 'Carte Vitale' — Vérifié le 18 novembre 2025

rows.authority: French bank (droit au compte: Banque de France)
rows.official_process_note: Needed for salary, CPAM reimbursements, rent and utilities. Banks ask for ID, the justificatif de domicile and proof of income. If every bank refuses, the droit au compte procedure via the Banque de France obliges a designated bank to open a basic account.
rows.source_version: Service-Public fiche F2417 'Refus d'ouverture de compte bancaire : droit au compte' — Vérifié le 28 octobre 2025

rows.official_process_note: A first-time filer declares arrival to the local Service des impôts des particuliers; the numéro fiscal is issued, the impots.gouv.fr account can then be created, and that is what sets up prélèvement à la source. If you keep a Norwegian employer, the withholding route depends on the employer’s URSSAF position — see the field below.
rows.source_version: Service-Public fiche F369 'Impôt sur le revenu - Première déclaration de revenus' — Vérifié le 05 juin 2026

rows.name_en: Household Goods Import with Transfer-of-Residence Relief (franchise de déménagement)
rows.name_no: Innførsel av flyttegods med tollfritak (franchise de déménagement)
rows.official_process_note: Norway is EEA but NOT the EU customs union, so your goods are a customs IMPORT. Relief conditions (service-public.gouv.fr F492): residence outside the EU for at least 12 months, ownership and private use of the goods for at least 6 months, transfer of your principal residence to France, import within 12 months of installing in France, and no sale or letting of the goods for 12 months after entry. Bring the dated, signed, valued inventory in two copies (the FIRST shipment’s inventory must list everything, even if goods follow later) plus proof of Norwegian residence — a certificat de changement de résidence from the French consulate before you leave is the cleanest evidence.
rows.source_version: Service-Public fiche F492 'S'installer en France après avoir vécu dans un pays hors Union européenne : quels droits de douane ?' — Vérifié le 19 novembre 2025

rows.official_process_note: In-person appointment at the local Bürgeramt within 14 days of moving in — requires the landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung).
Issued automatically by post after Anmeldung — usually within 2–3 weeks. The employer needs it before the first payroll run.
Mandatory before the first work day — choose a statutory Krankenkasse and give the membership certificate to the employer.

rows.official_process_note: For a non-EEA skilled worker, confirm the qualification, any required professional authorisation, the concrete job offer and compliant pay/conditions before work begins; the UDI processing-time estimate previously stored here was undated and has been removed.
rows.description: Non-EEA nationals cannot legally start work in Norway without a residence permit for skilled workers. UDI processing typically takes 8–16 weeks — this is the single longest lead-time item in the whole move.
rows.notes: Blocks the entire move — nothing else matters if the permit is late.
rows.source_version: Utlendingsforskriften (FOR-2009-10-15-1286), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret FOR-2026-06-19-1132 / FOR-2026-06-25-1375

rows.name_en: Employer Letter for the UDI Application
rows.official_process_note: A concrete offer of work is a statutory condition for the work-residence route; prepare the signed offer or employment contract for the application file.
rows.description: UDI requires a formal offer/confirmation of employment from the Norwegian employer as part of the skilled-worker application. Prepare and send it early so it never blocks the permit file.
rows.notes: Feeds: UDI skilled-worker permit file.
rows.source_version: Utlendingsloven (LOV-2008-05-15-35), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret LOV-2026-06-19-50

rows.official_process_note: Confirm the passport is valid well beyond the move date — renewals from abroad add weeks.
rows.description: Confirm the employee's passport is valid well beyond the move date. Renewals from abroad add weeks — check now, not at the airport.

rows.official_process_note: Check whether the role is legally regulated. Where law or regulation imposes qualification requirements, obtain approval or authorisation from the relevant professional authority; NOKUT is not the universal decision-maker.
rows.description: Some roles require Norwegian recognition of foreign qualifications (NOKUT or sector regulator). Confirm whether the role needs it and start the assessment now.
rows.source_version: Utlendingsforskriften (FOR-2009-10-15-1286), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret FOR-2026-06-19-1132 / FOR-2026-06-25-1375

rows.name_en: Norway is EEA, Not EU — Rule Briefing
rows.official_process_note: Review with the employee: an EU passport does NOT make Norwegian registrations automatic.
rows.description: Norway is in the EEA and Schengen, but NOT the EU. French employees (and HR) often assume intra-EU rules apply. Norway still requires a D-number, skattekort, and — for EEA nationals — police registration. None of these are automatic from an EU passport.
rows.notes: Core corridor quirk — the EEA-not-EU distinction drives most missed steps in this corridor.

rows.official_process_note: Start the housing search in the destination city — a Norwegian address is needed for several registrations later in the timeline.
rows.description: Start the housing search in the destination city. Rental markets in Oslo, Bergen and Stavanger move fast, and a Norwegian address is needed for several registrations later in the timeline.
rows.notes: Feeds: Folkeregister, lease deposit account.

rows.name_en: Supporting Documents — French Police Clearance & Medical Certificate
rows.official_process_note: Collect the casier judiciaire, a medical certificate if the role requires it, and certified translations where needed.
rows.description: Collect the documents the UDI application and onboarding may require: French police clearance (casier judiciaire), medical certificate if the role requires it, and certified translations where needed.
rows.notes: Feeds: UDI skilled-worker permit file.

rows.official_process_note: Private-school admissions dates vary by school and academic year. Verify the current intake window directly with each chosen school; this is planning work, not an authority-published process step.
rows.description: Families must hit fixed school application windows that close roughly six months before a summer move. Hard family flags: no French-curriculum school outside Oslo; no IB Diploma in Bergen for 16+; AIS has no DP until 2027.
rows.notes: Hard family feasibility gate — surface at offer stage, before the move is committed.

rows.official_process_note: The main coordinated municipal intake has a 1 March application deadline for an August start.
rows.description: Children under school age need a barnehage place, and the main municipal intake runs once a year — applications submitted after the 1 March deadline wait for scattered vacancies.
rows.notes: Family feasibility gate alongside the school window.

rows.official_process_note: Plan each accompanying family member’s own residence or registration route; the required registration depends on that person’s citizenship and status. Do not assume every dependant automatically needs a D-number.
rows.description: Accompanying spouse/partner and children each need their own D-number (and, for EEA nationals, their own police registration). Working only the employee's file leaves the family unregistered.
rows.notes: Mirrors the employee's D-number and EEA registration steps, per family member.
rows.source_version: Utlendingsloven (LOV-2008-05-15-35), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret LOV-2026-06-19-50

rows.official_process_note: Household-goods relief requires at least one year of continuous residence abroad, goods owned or possessed and used abroad, import within a reasonable time after moving, and the exemption request no later than customs clearance. Vehicles, professional equipment, food, drink, tobacco and nicotine goods are excluded.
rows.description: Unlike an intra-EU move, household goods shipped from France to Norway must clear customs. Duty-free flyttegods relief has strict conditions (≥1 year prior residence, owned and used goods, signed declaration, inventory) — prepare the paperwork with the mover before packing.
rows.notes: EU-customs-union variant of the EEA-not-EU quirk.
rows.source_version: Merverdiavgiftsforskriften (FOR-2009-12-15-1540), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret FOR-2026-06-26-1398

rows.official_process_note: For dogs, cats and ferrets travelling from France, verify microchip, valid rabies vaccination and EU pet-passport requirements. Dogs entering Norway also require Echinococcus treatment 24–120 hours before travel, recorded in the passport.
rows.description: Dogs and cats moving from France fall under Norway's EU-EEA-origin pet import rules. Requirements have fixed pre-travel windows, so the pet's paperwork must be planned alongside the move itself.
rows.notes: Rule source: pet_import_rules staging (Norway, EU-EEA origin group).
rows.source_version: Your Europe 'EU rules on travelling with pets and other animals' — Last checked 23/04/2026

rows.official_process_note: A used imported vehicle must be individually approved by Statens vegvesen before one-off tax can be calculated, and the tax must be paid before registration. Price the approval and tax before deciding to ship the vehicle.
rows.description: Bringing a vehicle into Norway is a taxed import, not a free EU transfer. Evaluate import duty, approval and re-registration costs before committing the car to the shipment.
rows.notes: Several corridor movers (AGS, Grospiron) handle vehicle transfer when the decision is to import.
rows.source_version: Engangsavgiftsforskriften (FOR-2001-03-19-268), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret FOR-2026-01-13-29

rows.official_process_note: Norwegian banks require a D-number before opening an account; payroll cannot be paid to a foreign account long-term.
rows.description: Norwegian banks require a D-number before opening an account, and payroll cannot be paid to a foreign account long-term. Start as soon as the D-number is issued.
rows.notes: Requires: D-number. Feeds: lease deposit account, BankID.

rows.official_process_note: Confirm the employing entity is properly registered in the Brønnøysund Register Centre — A-melding and withholding registration depend on it.
rows.description: Confirm the employing entity is properly registered in the Brønnøysund Register Centre. Payroll reporting (A-melding) and withholding tax registration both depend on it.
rows.notes: Feeds: A-melding, withholding tax registration.
rows.source_version: brreg.no 'Norwegian-registered foreign business (NUF)' — Last updated 23 March 2026

rows.official_process_note: Mandatory monthly employer report of salary, tax deductions and employment — required from the first payroll month.
rows.description: A-melding is Norway's mandatory monthly employer report of salary, tax deductions and employment to the authorities. It MUST be active before the first paycheck runs — setting it up after the fact is a compliance breach, not a formality.
rows.notes: Must be active before first paycheck.
rows.source_version: info.altinn.no 'A-melding – reporting salary and employees' — Last updated 18.03.2026

rows.official_process_note: Foreign employers posting workers to Norway report contracts and posted employees to the assignment register (RF-1198/RF-1199). Confirm whether the arrangement triggers it before work begins.
rows.description: Posted-worker arrangements (French employer keeping the employment while the employee works in Norway) trigger assignment-register reporting via RF-1198/RF-1199, alongside posted-worker notification duties. Confirm applicability with the tax advisor before the first work day.
rows.notes: Applies to the posted_worker persona; regular local hires by a Norwegian entity are out of scope for this step.
rows.source_file: docs/corridors/fr-no-supplier-dossier.md (tax gates: RF-1198/RF-1199, assignment register, posted-worker notifications)
rows.source_version: Skatteforvaltningsforskriften (FOR-2016-11-23-1360), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret FOR-2026-07-02-1489

rows.official_process_note: Assess whether the employee falls within the foreign-worker PAYE scheme and whether ordinary taxation should be elected. The stored 25% rate was not carried over because this source page does not print that annual rate.
rows.description: Register the employment for Norwegian withholding tax so deductions run correctly from the first payroll cycle. New foreign workers may qualify for the PAYE 25% flat-rate scheme — the ordinary-tax vs PAYE choice is made with the skattekort.
rows.notes: The PAYE vs ordinary-tax election is an individual tax determination — route to a regulated tax advisor.
rows.source_version: Skatteloven (LOV-1999-03-26-14), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret LOV-2026-06-23-66

rows.official_process_note: Norwegian lease deposits sit in a dedicated depositumskonto in the tenant's name — never transferred to the landlord's personal account.
rows.description: Norwegian rental deposits are held in a dedicated blocked deposit account (depositumskonto) opened in the tenant's name. It requires the Norwegian bank relationship, so it depends on the D-number chain — plan it before lease signature.
rows.notes: Requires: Norwegian bank account (→ D-number).

rows.official_process_note: Verify and document the employee's right to work in Norway before the start date.
rows.description: Verify and document the employee's right to work in Norway before the start date — permit or registered EEA residence, checked and filed.

rows.name_en: Payroll Readiness Gate — D-number + Active Skattekort
rows.official_process_note: Move-date gate check: payroll cannot run without BOTH the D-number and an active skattekort.
rows.description: Move-date gate check: payroll cannot run without BOTH the D-number and an active skattekort. Confirm both are in place today, before the first payroll cycle starts.
rows.notes: Payroll cannot run without both.

rows.official_process_note: Post-arrival check: confirm the police registration appointment actually happened and the confirmation document is on file.
rows.description: Post-arrival check: confirm the police registration appointment actually happened and the confirmation document is on file.
rows.source_version: Utlendingsloven (LOV-2008-05-15-35), lovdata consolidated text — Sist endret LOV-2026-06-19-50

rows.official_process_note: Norwegian digital identity for Altinn, tax services and government portals — usually obtained through the Norwegian bank.
rows.description: BankID is the digital identity that unlocks Altinn, tax services and most Norwegian portals — without it the employee keeps queueing in person. It is normally issued by the Norwegian bank, so it sits at the end of the D-number → bank account chain.
rows.notes: Requires: Norwegian bank account.

rows.official_process_note: Use Helsenorge to manage GP services, including changing GP. GP availability and waiting lists vary; the older dedicated GP-change page was last updated 12 August 2025, four days outside this gate’s freshness window, so its date was not reused.
rows.description: After Folkeregister registration, the employee can choose a general practitioner (fastlege) via helsenorge.no. Waiting lists vary by municipality — start early in Oslo and Bergen.
rows.notes: Requires: Folkeregister registration.
rows.source_version: Helsenorge 'Om Helsenorge' — Sist oppdatert 27. februar 2026

rows.name_en: Health Coverage Transition — CPAM Departure Notice → Folketrygden
rows.official_process_note: Notify the French CPAM of the departure and confirm Norwegian National Insurance (folketrygden) membership from the start of work — the health-cover handover is the step French movers most often leave dangling.
rows.description: Health cover must hand over cleanly between the two systems: notify the French CPAM of the departure, and confirm membership of the Norwegian National Insurance scheme (folketrygden) from the start of work in Norway. Posted workers keeping French cover follow the A1/S1 route instead.
rows.notes: France-exit step paired with Norwegian folketrygd membership. Cover-entitlement routing is a regulated determination — see the A1 step for the posted-worker variant.

rows.description: The valid identity card or passport an EEA national must hold for a right of residence (§ 111 første ledd) and present when registering with the police, which may additionally require the employer's confirmation of employment (§ 117 annet ledd).

rows.name_en: A1 certificate for a worker posted from France to Norway
rows.authority: Urssaf Service mobilité internationale — MSA for the agricultural scheme (règlement (CE) 883/2004 art. 12 §1; règlement (CE) 987/2009 art. 15)
rows.official_process_note: Initiated in France before departure, not in Norway: the French employer files the request with Urssaf Service mobilité internationale from its urssaf.fr employer account (régime général), or with the MSA for the agricultural scheme, and gives the employee portable document A1 once it is issued.
rows.description: The portable document A1 the French employer must obtain before the employee departs, certifying that French social security legislation continues to apply during the posting to Norway (règlement (CE) 883/2004 art. 12 §1; règlement (CE) 987/2009 art. 15), and the French institution the request is filed with — Urssaf Service mobilité internationale, or the MSA for the agricultural scheme.
rows.notes: Landed 2026-08-16 from the Otto counsel-attestation pack FR-NO-legal-2026-08-16.jsonl, NOT from data/corridor-facts/fr-no.json, so the corridor-facts loader does not manage it.
